gameStory.articleHeadline: Seahawks beat Raiders 21-13 as Drew Lock throws for 2 TDs and Seattle sacks Fernando Mendoza 6 times
gameStory.articleDescription: — Drew Lock passed for 240 yards and two touchdowns, including a game-breaking 71-yard scoring toss to Jaxon Smith-Njigba, and the Seattle Seahawks beat Las Vegas 21-13 on Sunday to spoil the debut start of Raiders rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza.
gameStory.articleStory: LAS VEGAS -- — Drew Lock passed for 240 yards and two touchdowns, including a game-breaking 71-yard scoring toss to Jaxon Smith-Njigba, and the Seattle Seahawks beat Las Vegas 21-13 on Sunday to spoil the debut start of Raiders rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza. The defending Super Bowl champion but injury-riddled Seahawks (6-4), playing their first regular-season game at Allegiant Stadium, have won three of four entering their bye week. Las Vegas (4-6), which lost standout tight end Brock Bowers to a right ankle injury, has lost six of seven. Facing Seattle's Dark Side defense, even in the venue known as the “Death Star,” figured to be a demanding obstacle for Mendoza. The top pick in this year's draft, elevated after Kirk Cousins was traded Tuesday to Minnesota, looked sharp early in leading the Raiders to 10 points on their first two drives. But then the Seahawks suffocated Mendoza, sacking him six times and holding him to 143 yards passing. Mendoza relied on his legs, rushing six times for 22 yards, including a 10-yard quarterback draw to punctuate the Raiders' first drive. Though Mendoza might one day become a star for the Raiders, Lock outdueled him while again filling in for injured starter Sam Darnold. Smith-Njigba will make just about any quarterback look good, and he finished with eight catches for 171 yards. His deep TD catch midway through the third quarter that gave the Seahawks a 21-10 lead. whatToWatch.text: Seattle's defense is the real deal — 18 points allowed per game and 2.3 sacks a night — and they're walking into a Raiders offense whose own defense is coughing up 29.8 per game. If the Seahawks ever wanted a get-right road trip, this is the matchup.

Five Seahawks are ruled out, and the names sting: Charles Cross, Leonard Williams and Quenton Nelson headline the list. Laying 6.5 on the road is a lot to ask from a shorthanded trench group — how the backups hold up is the whole ballgame.

A 40.5 total says Vegas expects a rock fight, and that suits a 5-4 club riding a one-game win streak just fine. The Raiders are down three of their own, including Thomas Booker IV and Dont'e Thornton Jr., so there's room to grind this one out and stack win number two.

recap.text: Drew Lock keeps proving he's no downgrade. Filling in again for the injured Sam Darnold, Lock threw for 240 yards and two scores in Seattle's 21-13 win at Allegiant Stadium, hitting Cooper Kupp from 34 yards in the first quarter and uncorking a 71-yard strike to Jaxon Smith-Njigba in the third that broke the game open. Jadarian Price's 12-yard run had already flipped the lead, and the defense did the rest, burying Raiders rookie Fernando Mendoza under six sacks and limiting him to 143 passing yards after he'd opened with 10 points on his first two drives. Seattle coughed up two turnovers and still never let Las Vegas back within one score, heading into the bye at 6-4 with three wins in its last four.

newsBlurb.text: Seattle heads to Allegiant Stadium with the Raiders thinner at quarterback, Las Vegas having shipped Kirk Cousins back to Minnesota for a 2027 third-rounder at the trade deadline. The Seahawks stood pat while their Week 10 opponent reshuffled its depth chart — now they get to see what that costs Vegas on Sunday.
